findings.note: tests/go/test-fsm.sh:9 reuses a pre-existing bin/metareview (`if [ -x bin/metareview ]; then MRV=... else go build ...`) rather than building unconditionally. Every other black-box script in tests/go builds a fresh binary into a temp dir (test-pr-ready-review.sh:8, test-sharded-review.sh:11, test-override.sh:10, ...). Inside the full suite this is harmless: tests/run-all.sh runs tests/manifest/test-manifests.sh first, which executes `npm run build` (test-manifests.sh:101) and rebuilds bin/metareview from current source, and tests/coverage.sh:46 rebuilds it on exit, so it always exists and is current. The residual hazard is the standalone dev loop: `bash tests/go/test-fsm.sh` after editing internal/fsm silently exercises the binary left behind by the previous run and reports ok, which is a false green in the one black-box suite covering the new FSM surface. Low, not medium, because CI and `npm test` both rebuild first.

findings.note: The injection section of tests/go/test-fsm.sh is titled 'fenced values never appear raw in instructions' and plants a payload that opens with the literal fence sentinel `<<<END-0123456789abcdef`, but its only assertion is that some audit entry of type llm_call exists (`const call=lines.find(e=>e.type==="llm_call"); if(!call) throw new Error("no llm_call")`); the bound variable is never used again and nothing checks that the payload was fenced or JSON-escaped in the emitted instructions. The section would stay green if fencing regressed entirely. Not higher than low because the property is genuinely covered at unit level: internal/fsm/judge/judge_test.go:97 and :129 feed exactly this spoofed sentinel and assert it does not survive verbatim, judge_test.go:734 asserts FenceBlock JSON-escapes it, and prompts.go:152 marshals the value rather than interpolating it.

findings.note: The forbidden-phrase check in tests/go/test-fsm.sh greps a hard-coded path list (`skills commands docs/fsm README.md INSTALL.md docs/quickstart.md AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md workflows`) with `2>/dev/null`. grep exits 2 with 'No such file or directory' when a path disappears, and the `if` treats any nonzero exit as 'phrase absent', so renaming or moving any of those paths silently downgrades the check to a permanent pass instead of failing loudly. The planted control immediately above only proves the regex matches, not that the path list still resolves; all nine paths do exist today.

findings.note: Ordering assertion in TestReviewLogListsIngestedAndIgnoredResults is vacuous if the verdict heading ever changes: `verdictAt := strings.Index(text, "## Verdict")` is -1 when the heading is absent, and the guarded comparison `shardedAt < verdictAt` is then false for any present sharded section, so the test passes while asserting nothing. Cheap fix would be to require verdictAt >= 0 first; no behavioural impact today.

findings.note: Override reasons are validated only for length (>= 12 after trimming, internal/findings/override.go:120-124 and :95-99) and are rendered straight into the one-line-per-record Markdown of the Process Overrides section (override.go:177-196, spliced by findings.go:317). A reason containing a newline therefore breaks the line format and can forge additional entries in docs/metareview/FINDINGS.md, e.g. a request whose reason embeds `\n- mrvf-000001 [granted] ...`. The audit file is human-facing and is also fed into context packs (internal/prready/review.go:165 and the other three gates), so the forged lines read as real records. Kept at low because the module documents `By` as audit metadata rather than authentication, and the actor able to pass the reason can already edit the file; a newline/control-character reject in the two validators would close it.
